workbench/page_marks.py (new). Page() runs every page through doorway.scan first. pattern_pass() needs no model: it finds every number with its own unit, amount, date, period and cue word on open lines, labelled from the line (leader dots, clause number with heading, a table row's first worded cell, 'Label:') or else from the heading, and passes each mark through the same checks as the model's. check() takes the model's marks in the design's order, with exactly one refusal reason each: NOT_IN_SHAPE, LINE_OUT_OF_RANGE, LINE_FLAGGED, KIND_NOT_IN_PACK, VALUE_NOT_ON_LINE (NFKC, spaces as one, with offsets), NOT_A_NUMBER, NUMBER_WITHOUT_ITS_OWN_UNIT (the unit must stand next to the number with no other number between), PERIOD_WITHOUT_A_TIME_UNIT, DATE_DOES_NOT_PARSE (an ambiguous date gives 'cannot tell'), MONEY_NOT_A_DECIMAL, NO_CUE_WORD, USES_WITHHELD_WORDS, SUBJECT_FROM_ANOTHER_ROW, DUPLICATE, OVER_EIGHT. The line's own label replaces the model's subject. A model subject whose words are on no row is kept as a ModelSaid, marked "the model's words".

The MARKS TurnKind, registered with turns.py (E0) on the 'reading' switch: caps 1000 new tokens, 140 answer tokens, 20 s; paper PAGES. Message 1 is one fixed brief that lists every kind. Message 2 is doorway.page_message, with flagged lines withheld. Message 4 names the pack's kinds. The per-request GBNF admits NONE, or 1 to 8 rows of the form 'L<n> <kind> | text | text'. It allows only the page's open line numbers and the pack's kinds, and single spaces only (grammars.check accepts it). Rows are parsed one at a time, so a malformed row is refused alone. The verdict is TAKEN, TRIMMED or REFUSED. The fallback is PATTERNS, the pattern pass.

ledger.pencil/1 is stored as Project Desk records of kind 'pencil', as pinned quotes are kind 'quote'. Each record holds the source (namespace, item, name, sha256, segment, locator, decision, extractor hash), page_sha256, the doorway rules digest, the line and line_sha256, a rect (PDF pages only, from quotes.page and quotes.located), kind, label and its source, a model label as ModelSaid.for_record, the value (always the page's own characters), offsets, a reading (exact decimal strings, never floats), the origin (PATTERN{rule hash} or MODEL{model, prompt digest, turn, kind ident}), checks, state and mark_digest. The id is derived from the content, so reading a page again adds no duplicate. record_digest() leaves out volatile fields. reanchor(record, text) gives CURRENT, MOVED (the same line at another number, or the same value under the same own label) or GONE.

decisions: Pencil records are Project Desk records of kind 'pencil' with schema ledger.pencil/1, as 0.8.6 stores pinned quotes. This gives them history and events, which Undo uses, and makes 'no other kind of record changed' a count by kind.

The pattern pass always runs on the press, and the model's marks are added after their check. A model mark that covers exactly the span of a desk mark is not written twice; it is counted as 'agreed with the desk'. Refusals counted as 'rubbed out by the desk' exclude DUPLICATE.

A number range written inside the value with a joining word ('2.7 to 5.5 V', or an en dash) shares the unit after its last number. A lone number whose next token is another number is refused, as in the design. When the unit stands just outside the value, the stored value grows to include it ('5.5' becomes '5.5 V'), so the value is always the page's own characters.
A unit outside 0.8.5's units table (°C, %, ohm and so on), or a compound unit ('25 mA per °C'), keeps the mark as words, not a quantity, as 3.4 says.

Subjects, where the design is loose: the line's own label always wins. A subject using words found only on another row is refused (the acceptance example). A subject whose words are on this line, its heading or no row at all is kept, but held as ModelSaid and shown as "the model's words", never as her words. The rule that the model's words are never shown as hers outranks the lens's phrase 'her words'.

The MARKS brief must be the same for every page, because turns.py requires a fixed brief. So message 1 lists every kind once and message 4 names the page's pack; the grammar still admits only the pack's kinds. The brief was shortened to fit the 1,000 new-token cap on the stand-in tokenizer.

Open question 2's default holds: a page reaches the model only through library.read, the press of 'Read this page', and only through the doorway's view. A page with every line withheld is not sent (ALL_WITHHELD).
